name: Sacsayhuamán
summary: The Inca walls above Cusco, the Rodadero outcrop and the city's houses, in one satellite pass: what each method draws over megalithic walls, beside houses and open fields.

frame.axes: x east, y north, z up; metres
frame.geoid_source: EGM2008 undulation at the origin, 46.19 m, through PROJ 9.5.1 (us_nga_egm08_25) and pyproj 3.7.2

terrain.source: Copernicus GLO-30 DSM, tile Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_S14_00_W072_00_DEM, resampled bilinearly from 1 arc-second

landmarks.name: The zigzag walls
landmarks.what: three tiers of Inca terrace walls; "The longest of the three walls is about 400 meters. They are about 6 meters tall" (Wikipedia)
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap ways 431479258 and 431479257 ("Murallas de Sacsayhuamán", barrier=retaining_wall), the midpoint of their extent; © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: Muyuqmarka
landmarks.what: the round tower's foundations on the hilltop behind the walls
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap way 480267375 (historic=castle), its centre; © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: Rodadero (Suchuna)
landmarks.what: the outcrop across the esplanade from the walls, with carved seats ("Trono del Inka", node 5857165093)
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap node 5857164644 ("Suchuna"); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: Chinkana Chica
landmarks.what: a short passage through the rock north of the Rodadero
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap node 5857164643 ("Chinkana Chica"); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: Cristo Blanco
landmarks.what: the statue on Pukamuqu hill, east of the walls
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap node 4746310711 ("Cristo Blanco"); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: San Blas church
landmarks.what: the church at the heart of the San Blas quarter's houses
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap way 23799145 ("San Blas", amenity=place_of_worship); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

landmarks.name: Plaza de Armas
landmarks.what: the city's main square, colonial buildings on Inca foundations round it
landmarks.source: OpenStreetMap node 6266294785 ("Plaza de Armas"); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), read through the Overpass API on 29 September 2026

notes: No structure is claimed beneath this site. It is composed for the satellite methods, to set megalithic walls beside houses and open hillside in one image.
The rock beneath is assumed limestone, as the walls' largest blocks are ("the largest Limestone block", Wikipedia); it is not surveyed, and no run here uses it.
Terrain is a DSM: the walls, houses and trees are in it, blurred over its 30 m cells.

sources.wikipedia: Wikipedia, Sacsayhuamán: coordinates "13°30′28″S 71°58′56″W"; altitude "3,701 metres"; "The longest of the three walls is about 400 meters. They are about 6 meters tall."

sources.egm2008: EGM2008 geoid (NGA), grid us_nga_egm08_25 from cdn.proj.org, evaluated with PROJ 9.5.1

volumes.label: Satellite · the published method at Zigzag walls
volumes.method: The real 2025 ICEYE pass through the paper-style pipeline (50 half-band pairs, 32 px patches, grid-median correction, no selection gates, lambda_s 0.48 m): focused power on a log scale, depth relabelled as the claim does (repeat at 648 m), smoothed across the ground for display but not in depth; not the gated reconstruction
volumes.caption: columns where the registration wanders, as over open ground
